agree.reason: The letter names the GMP and LMS gaps itself and shows it understands that regulated documentation can't be cut, so a skeptical HR manager would probably give it a phone screen, though nothing proves the teacher can work on a plant floor.

honest.reason: Rightly drops the unsupported claim to cut training time in half, but '1,260 students' under procedures she wrote counts years before the 2019 program existed (about 980 would be accurate), and calling the new teachers 'experienced professionals' isn't in the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the seven safe years and 18 teachers trained, but it misstates the student total and misses stronger true forms: the pass-rate rise as 17 points (a 41% relative gain), and about 216 hours of adult training delivered.

right_comparison.reason: It never sets her against the obvious alternative, a candidate who already has GMP experience, and it doesn't say why a procedure-focused teacher could be the better hire.

qualification.reason: The 90-day onboarding review with a written proposal gives a date and a deliverable the reader can check, but it has no measurable target and doesn't say what happens if the proposal falls short.

objections.reason: It meets the reader's main objections, no regulated-industry experience, no GMP records and an unfamiliar LMS, with concrete steps like working with Quality before changing anything, and it doesn't raise any objection the brief already answers.

fit.reason: This is a proper one-page cover letter, but it deliberately leaves out the 'cut training time in half' line the user asked for and doesn't tell the user why.
